clue.text: Teasing harmful to the elderly?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as '...', something that does harm in old age

explanation.surface: A question whether mocking someone does damage to old people.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a split-word joke: BAD IN AGE, harmful in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Banter of a light mocking kind is what friends exchange when they tease each other.

clue.text: Way to cook top of beef-and rear

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of the word, uppermost in a down entry

parts.note: to rear is to raise, as children or livestock

explanation.surface: A method of cooking the best of the beef and the hindquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow cooking in a little liquid in a covered pot.

clue.text: Goes under, doctor admits

parts.note: to own up is to admit, so owns means admits

explanation.surface: A physician confesses that a patient is sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinks below water and dies there, or is overwhelmed.

clue.text: World character?

definitions.meaning: the natural world, the physical universe

explanation.surface: A question about global personality.
explanation.definitionFit: The phenomena of the physical world, and also innate disposition, as in human temperament.

clue.text: Straight on, perhaps, for the scary ride

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Keep going forwards to reach the frightening fairground attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairground attraction in which cars travel through a dark tunnel past spooky effects.

clue.text: Stoops of some Scandinavians, say

indicators.note: say tells us to hear the words as spoken, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: Danes are people from Denmark, a Scandinavian country

explanation.surface: A phrase about the stooping posture of certain Nordic people.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop, in the sense of lowering oneself to do something beneath one's dignity, is to condescend.

clue.text: Polish gentility

explanation.surface: Upper-class manners of a person from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P suggests the nationality; it is refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined grace and style, both polish and genteel refinement.

clue.text: Profit announced-and denied

parts.note: a gain is a profit
said means stated or announced

explanation.surface: A profit is declared and then contradicted.
explanation.definitionFit: Contradicted or refused to admit, an old word for opposed.

clue.text: A strain at night

parts.note: strain in its musical sense, a melody sung in the evening, not effort

explanation.surface: Some effort or stress felt during the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Music performed by a lover beneath a window in the evening.

clue.text: These days an alternative to fostering

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the current era of years
an option is one choice among others

explanation.surface: A remark that nowadays one family route replaces temporary foster care.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a child into one's family and raising them is close in sense to fostering.

clue.text: Elder rose in confusion

indicators.note: confusion signals that the letters of the preceding words are jumbled up

explanation.surface: An older man flushed red, flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose in' is the fodder, rearranged under 'confusion'.
explanation.definitionFit: An older person, or one of higher rank by age, is the one ahead in years.

clue.text: Notaries acting for young lady abroad

indicators.note: acting suggests the letters perform a new role, rearranged

explanation.surface: Lawyers who certify documents stand in for an unmarried woman overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish title for an unmarried girl, equivalent to Miss, used of a young woman in Spain.

clue.text: Endlessly praising a cake ingredient

indicators.note: endlessly tells us to drop the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone praises a component of a bake without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape, commonly added to fruit cake.

clue.text: Dr Johnson's authority for way of speaking a line

parts.note: diction is one's manner of enunciation
RY is short for railway, a railway line

explanation.surface: The great lexicographer's source for how to deliver a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson compiled the famous 1755 English reference work of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's great lexicon of 1755 was the standard reference for word meanings.

clue.text: Mind baby? That was the originalidea

parts.note: the brain is the organ of the mind
a child is a baby or offspring

explanation.surface: Someone tells a baby to be careful, then credits the concept's origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's own invention or creative notion, conceived in their head as if their offspring.

clue.text: Rascal discovered by Milan opera house wit

parts.note: La Scala is the opera house in Milan
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A rogue found by a comedian at La Scala.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous scamp or rogue, also spelt scallywag.

clue.text: Wader burning oxygen?

parts.note: flaming means on fire
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A wading bird set alight with gas?
explanation.walkthrough: Wader means a long-legged wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink long-legged bird that feeds standing in shallow water.

clue.text: Coming out, met Green staggering

indicators.note: staggering suggests unsteady movement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Leaving the pub, someone met a person named Green who was reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Arising or appearing, in the process of surfacing.

clue.text: One hundred old boys stir tea and backbite

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
alumni are former pupils of a school or college

indicators.note: stirring mixes up the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A hundred ex-pupils mix their drinks and gossip spitefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander or speak maliciously about someone behind their back.

clue.text: Describe great story in this newspaper?

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: DT is the Daily Telegraph, where the puzzle appeared
an epic is a long heroic tale

explanation.surface: Report a grand tale in the paper you are reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray or represent in words or pictures.

clue.text: American plant of the redskin?

parts.note: a New World plant whose fruit has a skin coloured red

explanation.surface: A dated question about a crop of Native American people.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as Native Americans; it means a fruit with red skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant native to the Americas bearing a red-skinned fruit.

clue.text: Potter about on Sunday and dance amorously

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: to mooch is to wander aimlessly

explanation.surface: Idle around on the weekend and then cuddle on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and cuddle, or sway close together while dancing slowly.

clue.text: The walls of Paris reveal foxy-faced creatures

parts.note: le is the French for the
murs is French for walls

explanation.surface: The Parisian city walls expose some animals with pointed snouts.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are French, signalled by 'of Paris'.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascan primates have pointed, fox-like muzzles.

clue.text: Open tome about Don Juan, for example

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unfold a big book about the legendary seducer.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Juan is Richard Strauss's orchestral work, not only the libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss wrote an orchestral piece of that name, a symphonic work depicting a story.

clue.text: Off-season for Gloucester's opener

definitions.meaning: the cold quiet time of year when tourism stops
Richard, Duke of Gloucester, opens Shakespeare's Richard III with 'Now is the ___ of our discontent'

explanation.surface: Gloucester's first batsman is unavailable in the closed months.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Gloucestershire cricket; it is Shakespeare's Richard III.
explanation.definitionFit: The coldest season is the slack time for resorts, and the word starts Richard's famous opening speech.

clue.text: English river is a party to a night-attack

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge
taken as written
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A river in England takes part in a surprise assault after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical military term for an assault made at night, soldiers wearing shirts over armour to recognise one another.

clue.text: This artist got it right with a circle!

indicators.note: set right, the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: A painter succeeded in drawing a perfect ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says this artist proved his skill by drawing a perfect circle freehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Florentine painter of the early fourteenth century, famed for the Arena Chapel frescoes.

clue.text: Should one see the dentist with it?

definitions.text: Should one see the dentist with it?

parts.words: Should one see the dentist with it?
parts.note: seeing with the eye, and visiting a dentist with a canine, both fit

explanation.surface: Asking whether a certain dental problem needs a visit to the dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine of the upper jaw, beneath the eye, so one sees with an eye.
